research.heading: Research
paragraphs: I am a senior at Swarthmore College studying computer science and cognitive science. I am interested in decision-making under uncertainty at several scales: how brains learn to sort what they hear, how people weigh risks when they use AI, and how faithfully language models reproduce the behavior of whole populations.

I work with [Prof. Sukrit Venkatagiri](https://www.sukritv.com/) on human-centered AI safety. My senior thesis, advised by Prof. Joshua Goldwyn, builds reinforcement-learning models of auditory decision-making using data from the [Geffen Lab](https://hosting.med.upenn.edu/hearing/) at Penn.

directions.title: Auditing simulated people
directions.text: Measuring where LLM social simulators drift from real populations, and which errors no amount of fitting can fix.

directions.title: Seeing AI risks clearly
directions.text: Systems that help people reason through scams, privacy, and security tradeoffs when they use or build with AI.

directions.title: How brains learn to decide
directions.text: Computational models of how learners form categories from sound.

items.title: ScamPilot: Simulating Conversations with LLMs to Protect Against Online Scams
Social simulation audit
items.description: An information-theoretic audit of LLM social simulators: where a simulated population drifts from real people, and the part of that error no amount of fitting can remove.

items.title: Reinforcement-learning models of auditory categorization learning
items.description: Models of how learners form categories from sound, fit to behavioral data from the [Geffen Lab](https://hosting.med.upenn.edu/hearing/) at Penn, with an interactive article walking through the analysis.

items.title: PromptSafe: multi-agent deliberation for end-user developers
items.description: Voice agents that speak for privacy, security, misuse, and the user's own interests help people who build apps with AI weigh the tradeoffs in what they are making.

items.title: Kickapoo to English machine translation
items.description: A rule-based translation pair for Kickapoo, a low-resource Algonquian language.
